triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: All four rules for the Brazil 301 heading 9903.05.01 (+25%) were gated from 2026-07-23, a day after the USTR notice's own DATES clause makes the additional duty applicable to entries on or after 12:01 eastern time on July 22, 2026, so entries on 07-22 escaped the duty.
triage.triage_notes: Four identical effective_from edits (rate parameter, heading predicate, general-rate and special-rate derived rules); formulas and the 9903.05.02-9903.05.09 exception are unchanged. Source verified: resolve_provision.py on us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-07-20/2026-14542 (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union) returns 'DATES: July 22, 2026: As set out in Annex I to this notice, the additional duty is applicable with respect to products that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 eastern time on July 22, 2026.' The PR body's 'Judgment calls' section notes the composition grid still opens the Brazil window on 07-23 because the grid has no 07-22 date, so the composition-level window was not aligned by this commit (composition rework landed in follow-up 3c991acc0). Companion test unchanged.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes nothing but the version window: all four rules' `effective_from` moves from '2026-07-23' to '2026-07-22', with formulas, the 0.25 rate, inputs, outputs and scope byte-identical, so it is neither mechanical (dates are explicitly excluded from that bucket) nor a new-coverage enhancement. The source settles it: FR 2026-14542, resolved through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, expression_date 2026-07-20), reads "DATES: July 22, 2026: As set out in Annex I to this notice, the additional duty is applicable with respect to products that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 eastern time on July 22, 2026", and Annex I inserts heading 9903.05.01 effective on that same instant — so the pre-fix 07-23 gate was a full day late and genuinely disagreed with the source, not a defensible policy choice. No competing kind fits: no rate, comparison strictness, clause, boolean, or entity/scope element changed, only the effective date, which is the definition of wrong_period_or_effective_date.
triage.verifier_notes: Independent in-repo corroboration: at this same commit the composition's `brazil_section_301_component_rate` carries a proof atom whose excerpt is the FR DATES clause ("...on or after 12:01 eastern time on July 22, 2026") while its own window still ran `effective_to: '2026-07-22'` / `effective_from: '2026-07-23'` — a self-contradicting encoding, and the merged PR body records it as a judgment call: "Brazil 301 window opens 2026-07-23 in the composition grid vs FR 2026-14542 DATES 2026-07-22 (grid has no 07-22 date; not exercised)." Two caveats for the reviewer, neither of which defeats the classification. (1) The repair is module-only: composition.yaml is not in this commit, so at 86d35779d9 the composed program still gated Brazil 301 from 07-23; the composition was only moved to `effective_from: '2026-07-22'` in the later commit 65997b4e4. So the reader's phrasing "entries on 07-22 escaped the duty" is exactly right about the module but was still true at program level after this commit. (2) The module's own cited source (us/statute/hts/9903.05.01) is timeless HTS text with no date in it; the July 22 basis lives in FR 2026-14542, which the module's proof atoms never cite. The date is therefore correct but ungrounded within the module — a provenance gap worth a separate note, not a reason to reclassify. The companion test brazil-9903-05-01.test.yaml was not touched, so the corrected boundary remains unexercised at module level.
